column1: //tour Formatting the nodes of a model
//step Formats | | Each node is drawn in a format: a set of colours and shapes. The tool chooses one for you but you can also choose your own.

//step The format column | The format column | An optional fourth column holds two format names joined by a vertical bar. The first sets the subject and the second the object. Either side can be left empty.
//sub Only the first time | The first time a node appears | A format only counts the first time a node appears. Later lines can leave the column empty.

//step Automatic formats | Automatic formats | Without a format column the tool chooses for you. Subjects are drawn as objects and plain values as literals. Notes and types and web links get their own formats.
//step Named formats | Named formats | These are some of the named formats. Follow the Every format link to see them all.
//step Font size | Font size | Adding "minus" -fs and a number to a format name sets the text size in pixels.
//step Dashed borders | Dashed borders | Adding two numbers sets a dashed border: the length of each dash and then the gap. A font size can come first.
//step Subgraph boxes | Subgraph boxes | A format name after the "double slash" //end line styles a subgraph box. The same endings work there too: this box ends with sg1-6-4.
